title: Guided practice A: major eras in early Michigan
subject: social-studies
lessonGoal: Use dates and events to explain the order of important steps toward Michigan statehood.
successCriteria: I can put events in time order.
I can use two dates as evidence.
I can explain that a timeline shows sequence but does not prove every cause.

vocabulary.definition: events placed in the order they happened
becoming a state in the United States
information that helps support an answer

sections.title: Question and context
sections.body:
How do dates help us tell the story of Michigan becoming a state?
A timeline is like a path of stepping-stones. Each date shows where one event belongs.

sections.title: Build background
sections.body: Michigan did not become a state in one day. First, it was organized as a U.S. territory. Later, people wrote a state constitution. Congress and the president completed the steps that admitted Michigan as a state.

sections.title: EXAMPLE evidence — a town library timeline
sections.body: This is an Academy-created practice example. It is not Michigan history.

rows: 2010 — Voters approved money for the building.
data.access_note: Read from the earliest year to the latest year.

sections.title: EXAMPLE — model timeline thinking
sections.directions: Watch how the example uses dates without claiming more than the timeline shows.

items.prompt: What can the library timeline support?

steps: Start with the question: What happened before the library opened?
Look earlier: the request came in 2008 and the money was approved in 2010.
Example claim: The vote happened after the request and before the opening.
Check the limit: the dates show order, but they do not tell every reason voters made their choice.

sections.title: Look at evidence — Michigan timeline
sections.body: These are short factual paraphrases, not quotations.

source.title: Michigan statehood timeline
source.creator: Manuel Academy synthesis
source.context: Compiled from the Library of Congress and United States Senate statehood pages.
source.source_type: Teacher-authored secondary timeline based on public government records
events: 1835 — Michigan voters approved a state constitution.
1836 — Congress passed a law that set conditions for admission.
January 26, 1837 — Michigan entered the Union as the 26th state.
source.limit: This short timeline does not explain every disagreement or every person's experience.

sections.title: Your turn — find the middle step
sections.directions: Use the dates in the Michigan timeline. Choose the event that happened after the territory was organized and before Michigan entered the Union.

items.prompt: Which event belongs between 1805 and January 26, 1837?

choices.label: Michigan voters approved a state constitution in 1835.
The Michigan Territory was organized in 1805.

sections.title: Feedback — check the dates, not just the event words
sections.body: If an event sounded important but did not fit between the two dates, return to the year beside it. The question asks about order. Point to 1805, then find a later date that is still earlier than 1837.

sections.title: Your turn — explain the path to statehood
sections.directions: Write two or three sentences. Use at least two dated events from the Michigan timeline.

items.prompt: How does the timeline show that statehood was a series of steps? Name one thing the timeline does not tell us.

reference.what_you_learned: Dates place the steps toward Michigan statehood in order.
reference.evidence_you_used: The 1805 territory date, the 1835 constitution date, the 1836 congressional step, and the 1837 statehood date.
